title: GitHub Actions
tagline: A workflow file is just a YAML recipe for 'when X happens on GitHub, run these commands on a fresh machine.'

concept.label: What
concept.text: GitHub Actions runs commands automatically in response to repo events (a push, a PR), defined in a YAML file.

concept.label: Why
concept.text: Manually remembering to run tests before every merge doesn't scale -- automation runs them on EVERY push, no exceptions.

concept.label: How
concept.text: A file at .github/workflows/*.yml defines: trigger (on:), a fresh virtual machine, and a list of steps to run on it.

concept.label: When
concept.text: Once you have anything worth checking automatically: tests, linting, a build step.

concept.label: Where
concept.text: The "green checkmark" you see on GitHub PRs everywhere is this running under the hood.

mnemonic.label: T.J.S.
mnemonic.text: Trigger (on:) -> Job (a fresh VM) -> Steps (the commands) -- the shape of every workflow file

sandboxNote.text: commit this file to a real GitHub repo and push -- the Actions tab on github.com is where you'll watch it actually run.

code:
# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Run tests

on:                              # TRIGGER: when should this run?
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:                          # JOB: runs on a fresh virtual machine
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:                       # STEPS: commands run in order, top to bottom
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4        # get your repo's code onto the VM first
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest                       # if this step fails, the whole run fails

cycle.title: Read the concept table once
cycle.text: The shape to memorise, not the exact syntax: trigger, then a job that gets a completely fresh machine, then steps that run on it top to bottom. Every workflow file, however complex, is this same shape.

cycle.title: Type the code yourself — no copy-paste
cycle.text: Adapt the example to a real (even tiny) project of yours, commit it to .github/workflows/, push, and watch it run on the Actions tab.
cycle.hint: The VM starts completely empty every time -- if a command works on your machine but fails in Actions, it's almost always because something you have installed locally isn't installed on that fresh VM.

cycle.title: Apply it to your own data
cycle.text: Make the workflow intentionally fail once (e.g. a broken test), push it, and watch the red X appear on GitHub -- then fix it and watch the same check turn green on the next push.

cycle.title: Reflect & note
cycle.text: What was in the Actions log when it failed? Was the error message enough to know what to fix?
cycle.placeholder: e.g. The log showed 'ModuleNotFoundError' for a package I use locally but forgot to add to requirements.txt -- the fresh VM had nothing pre-installed, which is exactly the point...

cycle.title: Tick off before moving on
checklist: I can describe the trigger/job/steps shape from memory.
I committed a real workflow file and watched it run on GitHub.
I watched a check fail (red X) on a real push.
I fixed it and watched the same check pass (green) afterward.
